where: Section 1 (paragraph 2, last sentence) and the figure caption and figure aria text
problem: The text says the figure shows that NOx climbs above 1900 K 'while soot falls, so both are low only below that temperature', and the caption says 'NOx is low only below about 1900 K, where soot has already fallen'. The plotted data contradict this: soot is 0.9 at 1500 K, 0.85 at 1700 K and 0.6 at 1900 K, so in the whole 'below 1900 K' range soot is high, not low. A student reading the sentence and then the graph will be confused, and the sentence misstates the physics: a temperature cut alone cannot give a low-soot, low-NOx window; soot is low only at high temperature, so the lean φ condition is what closes the window.
fix: Rewrite as: 'The figure shows the trade-off at a fixed rich φ: NOx climbs steeply above 1900 K while soot falls. NOx alone would be cured by cooling, and soot alone by raising temperature, so neither lever works by itself. The low-emission window needs the lean φ condition as well: only at φ below about 1 and T below about 1900 K are both low.' Fix the caption to the same wording.

problem: 'The high-soot region sits at φ > 1.' In the standard φ–T map the soot island is centred at much richer mixtures, roughly 2 < φ < 4 for 1500 K < T < 2500 K, with φ > 1 only the start of the rich, oxygen-poor side.
fix: Write: 'The high-soot region sits on the rich side, roughly φ above 2 in the standard φ–T map, and at 1500–2500 K.'

problem: The φ–T map is drawn in terms of local, in-cylinder equivalence ratio and local temperature, but the figure x-axis is labelled 'peak cycle temperature'. The two are not the same quantity and the section switches between them without saying so.
fix: Label the axis 'local in-cylinder temperature, K' and note that the map is a local-gas-property map, not a plot of bulk cycle peak temperature.

problem: 'They are used in research engines and in a few production petrol engines as a lean-burn mode' covers both HCCI and RCCI. HCCI has appeared in a small number of production petrol engines, but RCCI has not gone into production.
fix: Write: 'HCCI has appeared in a few production petrol engines as a lean-burn mode; RCCI so far exists only in research engines.'
